terms.gloss: young; a young man or woman
terms.grammar: adjective and noun, third declension; comparative junior
evidence: Quint. 4.2.42: est mihi fīlius juvenis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: A grown young person, by the Roman count between about twenty and forty (Lewis & Short); “younger” is minor nātū (see younger).

terms.gloss: young; a youth, a young man or woman
terms.comment: One still growing up, younger than a juvenis in the strict count, though the two overlap.
Of small children: cum parvus essēs, “when you were little” (see small).

phrases.latin: hic erit juvenis penes quem perfectī hujusce bellī laus est
phrases.english: this will be the young man who has the glory of finishing this war
a young man (roughly twenty to forty)

sources: Lewis & Short: juvenis · Lewis & Short: adulescens · Lewis & Short: parvus
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-livius, loci-cicero-philosophica), checked against the editions named there.
Citations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them and have not been checked against an edition.
